title: Flu and Seasonal Shots
hook: Some vaccines are a yearly habit, not a one-time event — because the viruses change, or immunity fades, and a fresh shot keeps protection current each season.
key_points: A flu shot is recommended every year for almost everyone aged 6 months and older.
Annual updates are needed because circulating flu strains change from year to year.
The best time is early fall, before flu activity picks up.
Seasonal vaccination lowers your risk of severe illness and protects vulnerable people around you.
content_html: Not every vaccine is a one-and-done. The flu shot is the classic example of a seasonal vaccine: you get it again each year, and there's a good reason why.
extra_html: The CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for nearly everyone aged 6 months and older. It has to be yearly for two reasons: the influenza viruses in circulation change from season to season, so the vaccine is reformulated to match the expected strains, and the protection it gives gradually fades over the months. The CDC suggests getting vaccinated in early fall, before flu activity ramps up, so immunity is strong through the peak. Beyond lowering your own odds of a miserable week — or a hospital stay — getting vaccinated also helps protect the people around you who are more vulnerable, like infants, older adults, and those with chronic illness. Other seasonal respiratory vaccines may be recommended depending on the year and your risk, which is worth checking with a provider.

source.name: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

related.title: Vaccines Adults Still Need
related.hook: Vaccination isn't just a childhood checklist. Protection from some shots fades, new ones are recommended with age, and a few need regular boosters.

related.title: Cold, Flu, or COVID?
related.hook: They share a lot of symptoms, but colds, flu, and COVID-19 differ in how fast they hit and how hard — and telling them apart can change what you do next.

related.title: The First mRNA Flu Vaccine Arrives This Season
related.hook: Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine — the first flu shot built on the same technology as the COVID vaccines — is now FDA-approved and ready for the coming flu season.

flashcards.explanation_html: Flu viruses evolve from season to season and vaccine-induced protection declines over months, so the vaccine is reformulated and given annually.

flashcards.prompt: When is the best time to get a flu shot, and who should get one?
flashcards.back_html: Early fall, before flu spreads. The CDC recommends it for nearly everyone 6 months and older, every season.
